answer: The reef multiplier is published, charged in cedar, and vertex lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2201 identities would post 1221 proofs and burn roughly 60 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
